findings.body: `round_len` is computed as `u32::try_from(round.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)`. If the round contains more than `u32::MAX` turns (theoretically possible on a 64‑bit platform where `Vec::len` returns `usize`), the count saturates and `turns` will be incremented by `u32::MAX` rather than the true number. The old code incremented `turns` by 1 for each turn individually, so it never suffered from this inaccuracy.  The fix depends on the type of `turns`; if it is `u64`, use `round.len() as u64` directly; if it is `u32`, the per‑turn increment pattern is safer. Consider adjusting the arithmetic to match the type without a fallback that silently loses precision.
findings.title: Use the exact round length instead of saturating at u32::MAX

value.summary: This pull request refactors the host loop to process a round of turns (multiple turns authorized by `HiveStep::Speak`) instead of a single turn per iteration. The logic appears correct for the round semantics, but there is a minor potential inaccuracy in the turn count arithmetic when the round length exceeds `u32::MAX`. Otherwise, the change is safe to merge.
